newsitem.title: USA: Drug approved to help some Alzheimer's symptoms.
newsitem.headline: Drug approved to help some Alzheimer's symptoms.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday approved a new drug that may help moderate some of the symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

The drug, Aricept (donepezil) is not a cure, and the FDA said it had not been shown to have an effect on the underlying cause of Alzheimer's. But the agency said it might "moderate some of the disease symptoms."
Aricept will be marketed by Eisai America Inc. of Teaneck, New Jersey, and Pfizer of New York.
It is the second drug approved for Alzheimer's symptoms. Tacrine (cognex), made by Warner Lambert, approved in 1993, slows down the progress of Alzheimer's in some patients. Neither is a cure.

Alzheimer's disease afflicts an estimated four million Americans, including former President Ronald Reagan, and millions more around the world. It is a progressive disorder, robbing people of their memory and cognitive abilities.

The FDA approval was based in part on a 30-week study that found that patients on Aricept did better on two assessment tests than those who did not take the drug. The tests measured such things as memory, language and reasoning abilities.
